title: SR-1.27 Done comes only from a passing verify
request: Closes G92 (issue #242) and the PROTECTED part of issue #243: contractList sets a signed contract's state to done whenever a file named contracts/closed/<id>.json exists (src/engine/contracts.mjs:262-265), and nothing checks what the file holds or who wrote it. PROTECTED covers only contracts/signed/ and contracts/keys/ (src/engine/vault.mjs:27), verify writes contracts/closed/ through the caller's own identity (contracts.mjs:248), and contracts/receipts/ is unprotected. So any token with write scope over contracts/**, including the token a paired device gets (src/engine/devices.mjs:85) and a cloud connector's (src/engine/oauth.mjs:17), takes a contract out of the Stop-hook gate and the pre-push gate with no contract.verified record, and can rewrite its receipts. Found by the SR-0.03 red-team round and reproduced on 31 October 2026 on the main source. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: QL-1.02. It is urgent: until it lands, a stopgap fix ahead of it needs the owner's approval. On a case-insensitive file system (macOS APFS, Windows) a case variant such as contracts/Signed/<id>.json also reaches a signed contract, because PROTECTED compares exact spelling. Sensitive path (contracts and tokens): the QL-1.03 checklist applies before merge. Also closes issue #247: contractCheckSignature joined an unchecked keyid into the key path (src/engine/contracts.mjs:203), so a forged signature verified with a key planted under contracts/drafts/.

tasks.title: Verify output is immutable to every caller
requirements: contracts/closed/ and contracts/receipts/ join PROTECTED; write, append and delete under either path are refused as immutable for every token, local or remote, owner included
verify writes the closed record and appends the receipt as internal writes, so its own output still lands

PROTECTED is matched on the folded path, Unicode NFC then toUpperCase() then toLowerCase(), so a case or long-s variant such as contracts/Signed/ or contracts/ſigned/ is refused like the exact spelling on every file system (issue #243: on a case-insensitive volume the variant reaches the protected file)
the refusal reaches MCP and HTTP callers as a 4xx naming the path as immutable, never a 500, and nothing is appended to the log by a refused call

PROTECTED is checked on the resolved target as well as the requested path: the folded path of fs.realpathSync.native of the target's parent folder, relative to the vault root, plus the file name, so an 8.3 short name (CONTRA~1), a case variant in any segment, and a directory symlink or junction inside the vault all count as the protected path
write, append and delete check PROTECTED before anything else, including the syncFromDisk that append runs first, so a refused call never logs

syncFromDisk and recover() never record a disk change under contracts/receipts/ or contracts/closed/ as a new version: a file there with history in this vault's log is restored from the log and the drift is reported; a file with no history (a clone, a restore, a pull from another computer) is left on disk unrecorded, since a close counts only through its signature and a receipt is informational

a refused write, append or delete under a protected path answers HTTP 409 with error immutable and the path in error_description, and MCP returns isError with text starting 'immutable:' and naming the path

tasks.title: State comes from the verify record, not a file
requirements: a signed contract is done when the log holds a contract.verified record for its id with ok true and the signed hash, or when contracts/closed/<id>.json is a close record whose signature verifies under the key that signed the contract and whose hash equals the signed hash; any other file under contracts/closed/ plays no part in contractList, contractGate or the pre-push gate

done is a fact about a past verify: a later failing verify of a done contract is recorded and reported but does not reopen it, because a scope criterion can fail later for changes made after the work landed
memev doctor lists every contract whose contracts/closed/<id>.json exists but which is not done under requirement 1, as a contract to verify again; nothing is rewritten or deleted
a vault written by the code at the base, whose contracts were closed by a real passing verify, reads them as done after the change

contractCheckSignature refuses any keyid that is not the 16-hex form keyId() produces, before the keyid touches a path, and accepts a signature only by the key whose keyid the contract.signed log record holds (or, with no such record, the keyid in <id>.sig.json, still 16-hex)

contract.verified records the signed contract's canonical hash and keyid; a verify counts toward done only when its hash equals the hash in the contract.signed record; a contract.verified record written before this change carries no hash and counts while the contract's signed files still verify under the keyid of its contract.signed record

verify writes contracts/closed/<id>.json as a close record: a DSSE envelope over {id, signed hash, ok: true, verified_at} made with the vault's contract key, so an honest close travels with the backup
the set of contracts with a counting pass survives a restart and an upgrade: it is rebuilt from the log on open or saved in graph.json with the snapshot's seq, never held only in memory
contractList and contractGate answer from that in-memory set, kept current by each contract.verified record, never from a log scan per call
with the daemon up, memev doctor relays the unverified-close check (the allow-list in doctor.mjs), and the check carries no fix: doctor --fix leaves the file and the log untouched
memev_contract_status with no arguments and the session-start card list a done contract whose latest verify failed, with the failing tasks of that verify

criteria.statement: Clone a vault from git and open it with a fresh .memev. In the source vault, contract A was closed by a passing verify and contract B has a hand-placed closed file. In the clone, A reads done because its close record carries a signature over the id, the signed contract's canonical hash and ok:true.
